# Motif translation

Use this branch for a noisy grid with a distinctive single-color motif amid zeros and another background color, especially when the grid appears to contain a seed object and translated copies.

Record the motif's colored-cell offsets from its bounding box. Search for legal translations whose motif positions all contain zeros, recoloring those matching positions with the motif color. Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros/background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation. When manual scanning is error-prone, use a small script to enumerate translations and construct candidate output grids. Account for seed shape and translations within bounds; allow rotation or reflection only if demonstrations support it. Validate all demonstrated changed and unchanged cells.

# Tile classification

Use this branch when full-width and full-height separator lines partition the grid into equal tiles and the output dimensions match the tile layout. Map each tile to one output cell. Use demonstrations to identify which in-tile feature or count determines that cell; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive.

For the observed pattern with color-8 separators and 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, emit 1 for a tile with at least two 2s and 3 otherwise. Treat this as a pattern-specific rule, not a general tile-classification assumption.

# Diagonal phases

Use this branch for sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field when demonstrations suggest the output fills the grid with periodic stripes.

Identify the invariant of the parallel lines: constant row−column for down-right diagonals, or row+column for down-left diagonals. Use zero-based row/column coordinates and verify the sign against observed output: `column−row` indexes down-right phases; `row+column` indexes down-left phases. Infer the smallest plausible period by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue. Use demo output to establish the complete color mapping when available; marker positions alone may not identify every residue. Color every cell from its phase, rather than preserving only sparse markers. Verify cells on several demonstrated lines and ensure the candidate reproduces every demo.

# Edge continuation

Use this branch when demonstrations show color 1 marking an absent continuation at a grid edge across repeated rows, bands, or motif copies.

Compare the repeated structures to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. The missing part may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Check every demo's changed and unchanged cells, and select repeated copies from that evidence—not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
